title: Tracing Agentic AI for Efficient and Secure Execution
unit: Connected Intelligence Unit, RISE Computer Science
summary: Develop methods and tools to trace and characterise agentic AI workloads, from the structure of an agent workflow down to how it uses the underlying system. The traces are then used to explore more efficient and secure execution, such as acceleration, offloading and isolation.
requirements: Good programming skills, especially Python, and an interest in computer systems and AI. Linux, distributed systems, performance profiling and machine learning are important.

title: Distributed and Federated AI for Autonomous Vehicles
location: Kista, Stockholm (on site at least 3 days a week)
summary: Two topics in the DREAM project on real-time federated learning for autonomous vehicles: federated self-supervised learning to reduce the need for annotations, or knowledge transfer between models with different architectures, sensors or hardware. Applications are reviewed as they come in.
requirements: Strong background in machine learning and computer vision, including deep learning and Python.
contact: Henrik Abrahamsson, henrik.abrahamsson@ri.se; Sima Sinaei, sima.sinaei@ri.se

title: FE model of perforations in corrugated board
unit: RISE, in collaboration with DS Smith
summary: Build a finite element model of how perforations tear when corrugated board packaging is opened, using commercial FE software, and validate it with physical tests. Applications are reviewed as they come in and the position may be filled early.
requirements: Strong background in numerical analysis, modelling and simulation, ideally solid mechanics or lightweight structures.

title: Bridging the sim-to-real gap for robot arms
summary: Use domain randomisation and synthetic data to train robot-arm policies, including vision-language-action models, that work on physical hardware. Combines analysis of randomisation strategies with validation on a real arm.
requirements: Finishing a master's in machine learning, or another field with added ML and programming courses. Send GitHub (if any), grades and CV.

title: Image representations in property valuation
unit: ML engineering, with a property valuation start-up
summary: Study which features from photos, floor plans and aerial images improve automated property valuation beyond tabular data. The aim is a validated improvement in a system that is in use.
requirements: Finishing a master's in machine learning, or another field with added ML and programming courses.

title: Open application: your own applied machine learning thesis
summary: Propose your own applied machine learning project, for example in healthcare, finance, NLP or computer vision, and describe the idea in your application.
requirements: Finishing a master's in machine learning, or another field with added ML and programming courses.

title: Making apps agent-ready
summary: Study what makes mobile apps usable by AI agents. Build a benchmark of realistic user tasks and compare how well agents complete them through accessibility trees, screenshots and declared interfaces such as App Intents.
requirements: Final-year master's student interested in mobile development, HCI or AI agents.

title: Generative UI in native apps
summary: Implement one native app feature under several model-to-interface contracts, from tightly constrained to fully generative, and compare them on validity, latency, cost, consistency, design conformance and safety.
requirements: Final-year master's student interested in mobile development, design systems or AI systems.

title: A capability benchmark for on-device AI models
summary: Benchmark on-device AI models on realistic tasks such as summarisation, OCR and visual search, and compare them with a cloud model. The result is a capability map and decision framework for choosing local, cloud or hybrid AI.
requirements: Final-year master's student interested in mobile development, edge AI or evaluation design.

title: Human vs. AI code review in pull requests
summary: An empirical study comparing comments from human reviewers and AI tools on real pull requests, to show where each is strongest and how AI review tools can support development teams.
requirements: Final-year master's student interested in software engineering, empirical research or human-AI collaboration.

title: Analysing table tennis with AI vision
summary: Compare classic computer vision pipelines, such as tracking and pose estimation, with vision-language models for analysing match footage. Build evaluation pipelines, a small annotated dataset and a prototype analysis tool.
requirements: Background in computer vision, machine learning or multimodal AI, with an interest in sports analytics and video data.

title: Master's thesis in computer vision and deep learning
summary: Thesis placement at a Swedish computer vision and machine learning company. You work with a mentor on a research question in computer vision and deep learning, from literature review and experiments to the written thesis.
requirements: Interest in deep learning and computer vision, self-motivation and fluent English. Apply with CV and cover letter.

title: Thesis topics in software engineering and AI for code (48 topics)
summary: A published list of 48 thesis topics in machine learning for code, high-integrity software and supply-chain security, and smart contracts, for example program repair with reinforcement learning, safety of coding agents and verifiable software bills of materials. The list was regenerated on 8 October 2026.
requirements: KTH students read the group's thesis guidelines and email Martin Monperrus. International students may also email.
contact: Martin Monperrus (email address on the topic page)
